nodes.label: CardVault README
nodes.rationale: Project exists to demonstrate full CRUD behind a real login system, as the Code Institute capstone checklist requires.

nodes.label: One CollectionEntry table with status field (OWNED/WANTED)
nodes.norm_label: one collectionentry table with status field (owned/wanted)
nodes.rationale: Replaces two near-identical tables, forms and view sets with one while still showing the same two user-facing lists.

nodes.label: Why simplify (six tables cut to four, CardSet restored)
nodes.norm_label: why simplify (six tables cut to four, cardset restored)
nodes.rationale: Original six-table draft was over-engineered for the checklist. Custom User dropped; CollectionItem and WishlistItem merged into one CollectionEntry with a status field; CardSet cut then restored because a set_name string had nowhere to hold set size, risked inconsistent spelling, and a table makes filter-by-set a foreign-key lookup.

nodes.label: Authentication settings (django-allauth, username and password only)
nodes.norm_label: authentication settings (django-allauth, username and password only)
nodes.rationale: No email address is collected, so there is nothing to verify and no email service to configure; the Forgot your password link is removed because reset works by email.

nodes.label: Design notes (palette, typography, layout)
nodes.rationale: Neutral greys and near-black primary colour so colourful card images stay the visual focus; one system font stack with two weights so it is easy to re-skin later.

nodes.label: One review per user per card (unique constraint)
nodes.norm_label: one review per user per card (unique constraint)
nodes.rationale: Unique on (user, card); the review form becomes an edit form once the user has already reviewed the card.

nodes.label: Rating 1 to 5 check constraint
nodes.rationale: A database check constraint backs up the field validators so a bad rating cannot be saved by any route.

nodes.label: Calls to action (Create account, Browse cards)
nodes.norm_label: calls to action (create account, browse cards)
nodes.rationale: When logged in, the second button reads 'Go to My Cards' instead of 'Browse cards'.

nodes.label: Registration validation states (username taken, weak password, password mismatch)
nodes.norm_label: registration validation states (username taken, weak password, password mismatch)
nodes.rationale: Errors are specific: the weak-password state names the broken rule rather than giving a generic failure.

nodes.label: Add to My Cards control (Owned/Wanted, quantity, Add)
nodes.norm_label: add to my cards control (owned/wanted, quantity, add)
nodes.rationale: One combined control covers both collection (Owned) and wishlist (Wanted) instead of separate buttons; when logged out the panel is replaced by 'Log in to add this card'.

nodes.label: Card entries table (card, set, status, qty, Edit/Remove actions)
nodes.norm_label: card entries table (card, set, status, qty, edit/remove actions)
nodes.rationale: On small screens the table becomes a stack of cards (see wireframe 07).

nodes.label: All / Owned / Wanted status tabs
nodes.rationale: A status filter switches the single table below, so collection and wishlist share one page.

nodes.label: Summary figures (total owned, unique owned, estimated value)
nodes.norm_label: summary figures (total owned, unique owned, estimated value)
nodes.rationale: Estimated value ignores Wanted cards and cards with no price.

nodes.label: Add / edit card entry form (status, quantity, notes)
nodes.norm_label: add / edit card entry form (status, quantity, notes)
nodes.rationale: One form serves both add and edit. A duplicate entry is rejected with a message telling the user to edit the existing entry, and quantity of zero or less is a validation error.

nodes.label: Message styles (success and error)
nodes.rationale: Messages are prefixed with the words 'Success:' or 'Error:' so meaning does not depend on colour alone.

nodes.label: Remove confirmation
nodes.rationale: Removal cannot be undone, so it is confirmed on a separate step with a Cancel option.

nodes.label: My Cards stacked rows (mobile)
nodes.rationale: At 360px a table would not fit, so each entry is shown as a stacked card with its own Edit and Remove buttons.

nodes.label: Quantity at least 1 check constraint
nodes.rationale: No longer owning a card means deleting the row, not quantity 0, which keeps 'do I own this card?' a simple existence check.

nodes.label: Could if: worth exploring later
nodes.rationale: Good ideas that need a new table or a genuinely new skill; worth a spike before committing.

nodes.label: REST API and separate front end
nodes.norm_label: rest api and separate front end

nodes.label: One list entry per user per card (unique on user, card)
nodes.norm_label: one list entry per user per card (unique on user, card)
nodes.rationale: Unique on (user, card) rather than (user, card, status): a card is OWNED or WANTED but never both, which makes Got it! a one-field status change instead of a move between tables.

nodes.norm_label: us09 filter cards by set and rarity

nodes.label: Hero section
nodes.rationale: States the site's purpose up front: track every Pokemon card you own and want - catalogue, collection, wishlist and reviews in one place.

nodes.label: CardVault navigation bar (Browse cards, Log in, Register / My Cards, Log out)
nodes.norm_label: cardvault navigation bar (browse cards, log in, register / my cards, log out)
nodes.rationale: Same header and footer on every screen; links change with login state (Log in/Register when logged out, My Cards/Logged in as/Log out when logged in).

nodes.label: Paginated card grid (name, set, number, rarity; Previous/Next)
nodes.norm_label: paginated card grid (name, set, number, rarity; previous/next)

nodes.norm_label: card details panel (name, set, number, rarity, market price, average rating)

nodes.label: Empty state with link to catalogue
nodes.norm_label: empty state with link to catalogue

nodes.label: Three sprints (Foundations, Core features, Reviews/polish/testing)
nodes.rationale: Work runs in epic order because later epics depend on earlier ones: accounts before My Cards CRUD, a seeded catalogue before reviews.

nodes.label: Populating the catalogue (JSON fixtures with explicit primary keys)
nodes.norm_label: populating the catalogue (json fixtures with explicit primary keys)
nodes.rationale: Fixtures are repeatable and easy to reset during testing; explicit primary keys mean loading twice updates rows instead of duplicating them.

nodes.label: US05 Keep my data private
nodes.rationale: Every private queryset is filtered by request.user so other users' IDs return 404 rather than exposing or changing records.

nodes.label: US26 Keep secrets and debug mode safe
nodes.norm_label: us26 keep secrets and debug mode safe

nodes.label: US27 Populate the card catalogue
nodes.rationale: A fixture is preferred over admin entry because it is easier to re-run after resetting the database.

nodes.label: US28 Manage data in Django admin
nodes.norm_label: us28 manage data in django admin

nodes.label: Automated testing (45 Django tests)
nodes.rationale: Ownership checks (user B cannot edit or delete user A's records) are the most important test in the suite because they are a security boundary, not just a feature.

nodes.label: Heroku deployment (app cardvault, Heroku Postgres essential-0)
nodes.norm_label: heroku deployment (app cardvault, heroku postgres essential-0)
nodes.rationale: The Procfile release line runs migrate on every deploy so the schema stays in sync without a manual step.

nodes.label: Validators (W3C HTML, Jigsaw CSS, flake8, Lighthouse, check --deploy)
nodes.norm_label: validators (w3c html, jigsaw css, flake8, lighthouse, check --deploy)

nodes.label: Usage of AI log (Claude for planning, building, debugging, tests)
nodes.norm_label: usage of ai log (claude for planning, building, debugging, tests)
nodes.rationale: AI used as a collaborator, not a replacement for understanding the code; specific log entries are what make the section credible to an assessor.

nodes.label: PEP8 and the models (79-character line wrapping)
nodes.norm_label: pep8 and the models (79-character line wrapping)
nodes.rationale: Model field definitions with several keyword arguments easily exceed 79 characters, so arguments are wrapped across lines and flake8 is run regularly.

nodes.label: Database settings (dj_database_url, ssl_require=not DEBUG)
nodes.rationale: ssl_require=not DEBUG enforces TLS to Heroku Postgres in production without breaking a local connection that has no TLS.

nodes.label: Production-only hardening (SSL redirect, secure cookies, HSTS)
nodes.norm_label: production-only hardening (ssl redirect, secure cookies, hsts)
nodes.rationale: Only switched on when DEBUG is False so local development over plain HTTP still works; check --deploy then reports no issues.

nodes.label: Secrets and debug settings (SECRET_KEY, DEBUG, ALLOWED_HOSTS)
nodes.norm_label: secrets and debug settings (secret_key, debug, allowed_hosts)
nodes.rationale: SECRET_KEY has no default so the app refuses to start rather than silently falling back to an insecure key; DEBUG defaults to False so forgetting to set it on Heroku fails safe rather than fails open.

nodes.label: Static files settings (Whitenoise hashed storage in production only)
nodes.norm_label: static files settings (whitenoise hashed storage in production only)
nodes.rationale: Heroku's filesystem is ephemeral with no separate static server, so Whitenoise serves static files; the hashed-filename storage needs collectstatic, which Heroku runs on build but runserver and manage.py test do not, so plain storage is used when DEBUG or TESTING.

nodes.label: Site navigation (logged-in / logged-out states, POST logout form)
nodes.norm_label: site navigation (logged-in / logged-out states, post logout form)

nodes.label: US03 Log out
nodes.rationale: Logout is a POST with a CSRF token because Django 5 does not allow logging out through a plain link.

nodes.label: US23 Read and use the site easily (accessibility)
nodes.norm_label: us23 read and use the site easily (accessibility)

nodes.label: Message display rules (icon and word, role=status / role=alert)
nodes.norm_label: message display rules (icon and word, role=status / role=alert)
nodes.rationale: Success and error are distinguished by an icon and a word as well as colour, never colour alone; role=status and role=alert make screen readers announce messages without the user needing to find them.

nodes.label: Suggested Django messages pattern (wording kept in one place)
nodes.norm_label: suggested django messages pattern (wording kept in one place)
nodes.rationale: Keep wording in one place so a tester checking the table against the running site checks the same strings the views use.
